claims.text: Combining enhanced-sampling free-energy calculations with machine-learning surrogate potentials will enable accurate and efficient determination of melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across diverse high-entropy alloys.
The targeted high-entropy alloys have multi-principal-element compositional complexity and disordered atomic arrangements.
The proposed surrogate potentials can capture atomistic free-energy landscapes over a broad compositional space.
The approach is applicable around the equilibrium melting transition for a diverse range of HEA compositions.
Solid–liquid free-energy differences provide the thermodynamic basis for identifying melting behavior.
Reliable solid–liquid free-energy calculations permit determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy.
Enhanced-sampling techniques capture rare-event dynamics associated with solid–liquid phase transitions.
Machine-learning surrogate models can accurately approximate the required interatomic potentials.
Machine-learning surrogate potentials drastically reduce the computational expense of the free-energy calculations.
The combined framework can predict melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change on melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
Predicted melting properties will agree with high-throughput experiments to within approximately 5–10% across a wide variety of HEAs.
Traditional calorimetric measurements are too slow for broad HEA-family assessment.
Standard molecular dynamics is too slow for broad HEA-family assessment.
CALPHAD has low efficiency when exploring the full composition and temperature space of multicomponent systems.
Pure CALPHAD approaches are inadequate for capturing multicomponent interactions relevant to the proposed task.
Extremely sluggish kinetics can reduce the reliability of the proposed equilibrium melting-property calculations.
Complex multiphase coexistence can reduce the reliability of the proposed method.
Sparse training data for machine-learning potentials can reduce reliability and require further calibration.
Quantitative performance depends on surrogate-potential accuracy and completeness of enhanced sampling.
Systematic deviations greater than 10% across multiple HEA systems would be treated as a decisive falsification of the approach.
